text: An Egyptian court has convicted journalist Lina Attalah and ordered the closure of independent news outlet Mada Masr, drawing condemnation from the Committee to Protect Journalists over the use of judicial proceedings to shut down press operations.

Governments across the MENA region continue to impose internet shutdowns during student exam periods, a practice documented in Access Now's latest report card tracking which countries have blocked connectivity in the name of preventing cheating.

Freedom House documents two apparent transnational repression incidents in Southeast Asia: a Laotian asylum seeker vanished near Bangkok with an alleged $8,000 bounty circulating online, while three Vietnamese activists were abducted from Cambodia and returned to Vietnam to face terrorism investigations — two holding Western residency or citizenship.

Freedom House's annual report finds global internet freedom has declined for 16 consecutive years, with authoritarian governments increasingly using AI-related laws, age-verification requirements, and network isolation measures to restrict online access and expression across 38 assessed countries.

Access Now reports that indefinite internet shutdowns are increasing year over year, with governments and other actors cutting entire populations off from connectivity with no stated endpoint or restoration plan.

Vietnam has imprisoned two journalists formerly affiliated with Voice of America — Le Anh Hung and Pham Chi Dung — in what Freedom House describes as part of a pattern of detaining and prosecuting independent journalists in one of the world's most restrictive media environments.

Access Now has written to four pension funds urging them to examine their exposure to AE Industrial Partners, which acquired spyware vendor Paragon Solutions in 2024 and merged it with surveillance contractor REDLattice.

Privacy International submitted a response to the UK government's consultation on workplace monitoring technologies, raising concerns about the expanding use of employer surveillance tools and calling for clearer legal limits on how workers can be tracked.

Freedom House has adopted the case of Tatiana Kouzina, a Belarusian civil society researcher imprisoned by the Lukashenka government, which the organization describes as systematically imprisoning independent experts and dissenting voices to eliminate credible sources of information outside state control.

Apple has sent threat notifications to users it suspects have been targeted by spyware since 2021, alerting them via email, iMessage, and account banners — a system Access Now has documented as a key tool for identifying state-sponsored spyware campaigns against journalists, activists, and others.
